children: The 10th edition of the prestigious BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026), hosted at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity, is bringing leading voices from across the hospitality industry for the next two days of conversations on the sector’s growth and evolution. With the theme ‘India’s Hospitality Decade: From Growth to Greatness’, the Summit will examine the opportunities, challenges and shifts shaping India’s hospitality landscape as the industry enters a defining decade.

The Brand Leadership Showcase – Chalet/Athiva Hotels & Resorts brought the company’s growth strategy and evolving hospitality portfolio into focus, exploring the opportunities shaping its next phase of expansion and the role of differentiated brands in India’s changing hospitality landscape.

Shwetank Singh, MD & CEO, Chalet Hotels Limited; Gaurav Singh, COO, Chalet Hotels; and Manoj Agarwal, Chief Growth & Product Officer, Chalet Hotels, shared their perspectives on the company’s growth trajectory, portfolio strategy and the opportunities emerging across India’s hospitality market.

Singh explained Chalet’s strategy of diversifying its portfolio across hospitality, leisure and commercial assets. He highlighted how the company’s commercial assets provided a stable income stream during the COVID period, supporting the business through a challenging phase.

“We wanted to diversify our eggs into different baskets. We decided to take up a few leisure destinations and also took a decision to bring in some commercial assets to our business, which was correctly proven during Covid,” said Shwetank Singh, MD & CEO, Chalet Hotels Limited.
“We were the only hospitality brand in the country that stayed in the black through the period, and we had a good annuity income coming throughout Covid,” he added.

Gaurav Singh introduced Athiva as Chalet’s new premium lifestyle brand, highlighting its early performance and its ambition to explore spaces that conventional hospitality has not traditionally addressed. He outlined joy, wellbeing and sustainability as the three pillars underpinning the brand.

“Athiva is a new-born baby of Chalet Hotels, which is just 10 months old. We have two hotels open so far, and with the first two hotels, we have received great feedback from customers,” said Gaurav Singh, COO, Chalet Hotels.

“We wanted to go into a space that hospitality hasn’t touched yet. We entered the premium lifestyle space, which was owned and operated by us, with the three basic pillars of Athiva being joy, wellbeing and sustainability,” he added.

Agarwal outlined Athiva’s measured growth strategy, emphasising the importance of building the brand thoughtfully while retaining a strong relationship with guests. He noted that the brand currently has 2,200 rooms in the pipeline, including around 1,200 additional keys, while Chalet is also exploring different models with international brands.

“We are carefully picking up the growth story for the Athiva brand. We think there’s real value in owning a guest relationship, and pacing the brand in a thoughtful manner is important for its long-term growth,” said Manoj Agarwal, Chief Growth & Product Officer, Chalet Hotels.
“We have 2,200 rooms right now under pipeline for the Athiva brand and are adding around 1,200 odd keys. We are comfortable with the pace, and the growth is following us,” he added.

The showcase wrapped up with a clear, sharp outline of Chalet Hotels’ path forward. Singh and his leadership team made it evident that maintaining their competitive edge relies on a tight balance, maximising yields across existing assets through operational discipline while aggressively pursuing smart, high-return expansion opportunities.

The two-day BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) encompasses over 25 sessions where hospitality veterans and experts across the nation gathered to provide diverse knowledge and insights. The Summit & Awards is a testament to BW Hotelier’s commitment towards revolutionising Indian hospitality by honouring the crème de la crème of the industry.
